title: Geo: Xi’s visit, regional flashpoints and a Gaza plan
summary: This edition keeps the earlier Xi visit report and adds four developments: renewed accusations and fighting in Tigray, a court ruling on White House press access, missing F-35 components under investigation, and a reported Gaza reconstruction plan. GDELT, ISW and Polymarket were unavailable; ReliefWeb returned no items.

stories.headline: Trump greets Xi Jinping at plane as Chinese leader arrives for state visit
stories.dek: Xi Jinping began a three-day US trip with trade and AI competition at the top of the agenda.
tldr: Trump greeted Xi Jinping at his plane as the Chinese leader arrived for a state visit, the Guardian reported.
Al Jazeera described a three-day US trip and said Trump is betting on stabilising global relations.
BBC said AI superpower ambitions were taking centre stage, and CNBC reported Bessent said the US-China trade truce had been extended for two months as the visit began.

body.text: Trump greeted Xi Jinping at his plane as the Chinese leader arrived for a state visit, the Guardian reported.
Al Jazeera reported the arrival as the start of a three-day US trip and said Trump is betting on stabilising global relations.
BBC said AI superpower ambitions were taking centre stage as the two leaders met.
The economic track moved first: CNBC reported Bessent said the US-China trade truce had been extended for two months as Xi began the visit.

stories.whyItMatters: The visit bundles trade, technology and security into one negotiation: a truce extension eases near-term tariff risk for markets, while AI rivalry keeps chips and supply chains on the table. It is the day's clearest cross-vertical signal.
stories.editorNote: Headline-level wire coverage; outcomes of the talks had not been reported at the time of collection. The trade-truce detail is covered in Markets.

stories.headline: Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war
stories.dek: Ethiopia’s federal government and Tigray’s regional authorities traded accusations of offensives, raising fears that the fragile peace may unravel.
tldr: BBC reported mutual accusations that each side had launched offensives.
DW separately described new fighting and fears of a return to civil war.
The collected reports establish competing claims, not an independently verified account of who initiated the fighting.

body.text: The BBC headline reports that Ethiopia and Tigray accused each other of launching offensives.
DW reported new fighting in the region and concern about a return to civil war.
The reports describe competing allegations; this edition does not present either side’s claim as independently verified.

stories.whyItMatters: Renewed fighting could threaten the peace framework and widen instability in the Horn of Africa.
stories.editorNote: Both sources report claims by opposing sides. No casualty figure or battlefield outcome is included because the collected coverage did not establish one.

stories.headline: US judge blocks Trump’s White House ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico
stories.dek: A federal judge blocked the White House restriction on access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico, according to two reports.
tldr: Al Jazeera reported that a judge blocked the White House ban affecting CNN, MS NOW and Politico.
CNBC reported that the judge lifted Trump’s ban on the three outlets.
The reports describe restored access; the collected headlines do not include the court’s reasoning.

body.text: Al Jazeera reported that a U.S. judge blocked Trump’s White House ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico.
CNBC reported the ruling as lifting the restriction on the three outlets.
The collected headlines do not specify the legal reasoning or subsequent appeal status.

stories.whyItMatters: The ruling concerns the boundary between executive control of press access and judicial review.
stories.editorNote: This is a headline-level account; no legal rationale is inferred.

stories.headline: Australia investigating how F-35 fighter jet parts bound for US went missing in Hong Kong
stories.dek: Australia is investigating missing F-35 components that were reportedly bound for the United States and went through Hong Kong.
tldr: The Guardian reported an Australian investigation into F-35 parts bound for the U.S. that went missing in Hong Kong.
CNBC separately reported that Chinese authorities were reportedly in possession of F-35 components in Hong Kong.
The reporting does not establish who handled the parts or how they went missing.

body.text: The Guardian reported that Australia was investigating how F-35 parts bound for the United States went missing in Hong Kong.
CNBC reported that Chinese authorities were reportedly in possession of F-35 components there.
The available headlines do not establish the chain of custody or confirm what happened to the components.

stories.whyItMatters: The case touches defense supply-chain security and U.S.-China tensions, but the public account remains incomplete.
stories.editorNote: “Reportedly” is retained from the coverage; no attribution of responsibility is made.

stories.headline: Trump's Board of Peace unveils $2.45bn plan to begin Gaza's reconstruction
stories.dek: The BBC reported that Trump’s Board of Peace unveiled a $2.45 billion plan to begin reconstruction in Gaza.
tldr: The BBC and DAWN reported that the Board of Peace announced a $2.45 billion Gaza reconstruction plan.
A separate UN-agency report in the collection described a rise in reports of violence against women in Gaza.
The collected material does not specify the plan’s funding commitments, timetable or implementation arrangements.

body.text: The BBC and DAWN reported that Trump’s Board of Peace unveiled a $2.45 billion plan to begin Gaza reconstruction.
The BBC also reported a UN agency finding of a surge in reports of violence against women in Gaza, a separate indicator of the humanitarian context.
No additional details about funding, oversight or implementation were present in the collected headlines.

stories.whyItMatters: The announcement places reconstruction financing alongside unresolved humanitarian conditions; implementation details will determine what changes on the ground.
stories.editorNote: The amount and description are attributed to the BBC headline. The UN-agency report is contextual, not evidence about the plan itself.
